libu.name: Libu
libu.summary: An ancient Libyan tribe of Berber origin, first recorded in Egyptian sources under Ramesses II and Merneptah in the 13th century BC, from whose name "Libya" derives.

ramesses-ii.name: Ramesses II
ramesses-ii.summary: Third pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty (c. 1303–1213 BC), often called Ramesses the Great; his 66-year reign, the longest of any pharaoh, included 15 military campaigns.

merneptah.name: Merneptah
merneptah.summary: Fourth pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, reigning for almost ten years from 1213 BC; son of Ramesses II, best known for the stele mentioning Israel.

tassili-n-ajjer.name: Tassili n'Ajjer
tassili-n-ajjer.summary: A Sahara Desert mountain range in southeastern Algeria holding one of the world's most important groupings of prehistoric cave art, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

bell-beaker-culture.name: Bell Beaker culture
bell-beaker-culture.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological culture named for its inverted-bell drinking vessel, spreading across Western Europe from around 2800 BCE.

tagus.name: Tagus
tagus.summary: The longest river in the Iberian Peninsula, rising in Spain and flowing about 1,007 km westward to the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon.

garamantes.name: Garamantes
garamantes.summary: An ancient people, likely descended from Berber and Saharan groups, who built a desert kingdom in Libya's Fezzan region from around 1000 BCE using irrigation to farm and control trade.

fezzan.name: Fezzan
fezzan.summary: The desert region of southwestern Libya, dotted with oases amid the Sahara, later designated one of Libya's three main provinces after 1934.

germa.name: Germa
germa.summary: An archaeological site in Libya, known in ancient times as Garama, that served as capital of the Garamantian Kingdom.

dhar-tichitt.name: Dhar Tichitt
dhar-tichitt.summary: A line of sandstone cliffs in southwestern Mauritania with Neolithic sites inhabited by pastoralists and farmers between about 2000 and 300 BCE, among the oldest known settlements in West Africa.

sea-peoples.name: Sea Peoples
sea-peoples.summary: A group of tribes who raided Egypt and other eastern Mediterranean regions around 1200 BC, once seen as a main cause of the Bronze Age collapse but now often viewed as refugees fleeing an ongoing crisis.

meryey.name: Meryey
meryey.summary: A Berber king and Great Chief of the Libu in the late 13th century BC, who organized a military alliance with other Libyan groups and Sea Peoples against pharaoh Merneptah.

meshwesh.name: Meshwesh
meshwesh.summary: An ancient Libyan tribe first recorded under pharaoh Amenhotep III around 1390-1350 BC, later often at war with Egypt and eventually ruling it during the 22nd and 23rd Dynasties.

eighteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt
eighteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: The first dynasty of Egypt's New Kingdom (1550–1292 BC), the era of Egypt's peak power, including pharaohs Tutankhamun, Hatshepsut and Akhenaten.

amenhotep-iii.name: Amenhotep III
amenhotep-iii.summary: Ninth pharaoh of Egypt's 18th Dynasty, ruling around 1386–1349 BC during a peak of Egyptian wealth and influence; father of Akhenaten.

merneptah-stele.name: Merneptah Stele
merneptah-stele.summary: An Egyptian inscription by pharaoh Merneptah, discovered in 1896, chiefly recording his victory over the Libyans but also containing the earliest known textual mention of Israel.

nineteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.name: 19th Dynasty
nineteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: The second dynasty of Egypt's New Kingdom, lasting from 1292 to 1189 BC, founded by Ramesses I and part of what is called the Ramesside period.

oric-bates.name: Oric Bates
oric-bates.summary: American archaeologist and author (1883–1918) who led expeditions in Libya and Sudan and directed the Egyptian Department at Boston's Museum of Fine Arts.

cyrenaica.name: Cyrenaica
cyrenaica.summary: Eastern region of Libya named for the ancient city of Cyrene, once part of the Roman province of Crete and Cyrenaica and later Libya's Barqa region under Islamic rule.

marsa-matrouh.name: Marsa Matrouh
marsa-matrouh.summary: A port city in Egypt, west of Alexandria, that was a major grain port under the Romans and later a British military base; fighting took place there during World War II.

great-karnak-inscription.name: Great Karnak Inscription
great-karnak-inscription.summary: A 79-line hieroglyphic inscription at Karnak recording pharaoh Merneptah's campaign against the Sea Peoples at the Battle of Perire; it is the longest surviving continuous monumental text from Egypt.

lukka-lands.name: Lukka lands
lukka-lands.summary: Ancient region of Anatolia known from Hittite and Egyptian texts, which viewed its people as hostile. The name is commonly accepted as related to Lycia of classical antiquity.

ramesses-iii.name: Ramesses III
ramesses-iii.summary: Second pharaoh of Egypt's Twentieth Dynasty, reigning roughly 1185 to 1154 BC; the last New Kingdom pharaoh with real power, he defeated the Sea Peoples but was later assassinated in a harem conspiracy.

malkata.name: Malkata
malkata.summary: Site of an ancient Egyptian palace complex built in the New Kingdom by Amenhotep III, on the Nile's West Bank at Thebes. It also had a temple for his Great Royal Wife, Tiy.

nine-bows.name: Nine Bows
nine-bows.summary: Ancient Egyptian visual symbol standing for foreigners and enemies of Egypt, with no fixed list of peoples. The number nine expressed totality, and the bows may also have represented disorder.

philistus.name: Philistus
philistus.summary: Greek historian from Sicily who lived c. 432 to 356 BC.

timaeus-historian.name: Timaeus of Tauromenium
timaeus-historian.summary: Ancient Greek historian (c. 356/350–260 BC) regarded as the leading authority on the history of the Greek West for centuries.

carthage.name: Carthage
carthage.summary: Ancient city in what is now Tunisia, a major Mediterranean trading hub and capital of a Punic empire. Rome destroyed it in 146 BC at the end of the Third Punic War.

akhenaten.name: Akhenaten
akhenaten.summary: An ancient Egyptian pharaoh who reigned around 1353 to 1336 BC and abandoned traditional polytheism to introduce worship centered on the sun god Aten, a change reversed after his death.

seti-i.name: Seti I
seti-i.summary: Second pharaoh of Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty, ruling from 1290 BC to 1279 BC in the New Kingdom. Son of Ramesses I and father of Ramesses II, known as Ramesses the Great.

karnak.name: Karnak
karnak.summary: A vast temple complex near Luxor, Egypt, begun under Senusret I around 1971-1926 BC and expanded through the Ptolemaic period, serving as the main place of worship of the god Amun.

mechta-afalou.name: Mechta-Afalou
mechta-afalou.summary: A population that lived in North Africa during the late Paleolithic and Mesolithic, linked to the Iberomaurusian culture and named after a burial site in Béjaïa, Algeria, later absorbed by Capsian-culture peoples.

capsian.name: Capsian
capsian.summary: An Epipalaeolithic culture of Algeria and Tunisia from about 9000 to 5400 BCE, named after the town of Gafsa, known for a varied hunting diet and early decorative art.
